# Independent deterministic reproduction, plus a SECOND harm this ticket does not yet record

From the Phase-1 investigation of bug `f0fb-de7a-b315-4508` (`nonodorous-snotty-seaurchin`,
"Detached (nohup) pytest runs report errors that do not reproduce in a foreground shell").
That investigation's proven root cause IS this fixture, so the evidence belongs here too.

## Deterministic reproduction (1/1)

Worktree off `origin/main` at `987caf8c73`. Start a detached pytest run, then — from a
separate shell, 4 seconds in — make a single external write that no test touches:

    nohup env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest \
      tests/integration/test_reclaim_bridge_history.py -q > /tmp/log 2>&1 < /dev/null &
    sleep 4
    touch /Users/joeoakhart/<worktree>/EXTERNAL_MUTATION_PROBE

Observed:

    E  Failed: Test leaked new entries into REPO_ROOT (use tmp_path or a sandboxed temp dir):
       ['EXTERNAL_MUTATION_PROBE']
    tests/conftest.py:322: Failed
    ERROR tests/integration/test_reclaim_bridge_history.py::test_cli_never_invokes_push_and_leaves_source_refs_exact
    6 passed, 1 error in 7.55s

Afterwards the probe file was **gone** — `tests/conftest.py:316` `target.unlink()` had removed
it. That is the deletion harm this ticket already records, reproduced on demand.

## The second harm: it fails an INNOCENT test and the message asserts a falsehood

`test_cli_never_invokes_push_and_leaves_source_refs_exact` did nothing wrong. It neither
created nor touched `EXTERNAL_MUTATION_PROBE`. The fixture attributes the entry to whichever
test happened to straddle the external write — arbitrary, and a different test on each run.
The message it then emits is a false statement of fact:

    "Test leaked new entries into REPO_ROOT (use tmp_path or a sandboxed temp dir)"

No test leaked anything. The text names a cause that did not occur and prescribes a remedy
(`use tmp_path`) for a defect the test does not have.

**This is arguably worse than the deletion**, because it is actively misleading rather than
merely destructive: it sends a debugger after the wrong test. Concretely, in ticket `f0fb` an
agent landing Gerrit 1943 recorded that it "nearly chased those as real regressions", and
filed the whole effect as a mystery property of `nohup`. It is not: detachment is only the
mode in which a concurrent external actor can exist at all (a foreground run blocks the agent
that would otherwise be mutating the checkout). 15 detached runs at load average 9-13 with
`stdin=/dev/null` and no controlling terminal were **entirely clean**; the failure appears
only when something external writes to `REPO_ROOT` mid-run.

So the attribute-before-deleting question in this ticket's acceptance criteria has a twin that
is worth covering explicitly: **attribute-before-BLAMING**. Whatever mechanism decides that an
entry is not the test's should also govern what the failure message claims, not just whether
the file is removed. An entry the fixture cannot attribute should not produce a message that
asserts a test leaked it.

## Prior sightings of this same environmental false positive (not new, and recurring)

- `f8a2-bf40-4cc4-479b` (closed) — "bash-suite REPO_ROOT leak (.tickets-tracker) + macOS
  tmp-cleaner race": a non-test external actor tripping this guard, filed and fixed as a bug.
- `3a03-9863-542e-4ae1` (closed) — a prior fix to this same fixture.
- Ticket `5ac8` records: "1 environmental teardown artifact (.tickets-tracker symlink flagged
  by the REPO_ROOT leak detector under the make-worktree store symlink; the test passes in
  isolation and is unrelated to the version bump)."
- A session log records: "Pre-existing on main, not ours: `test_plan_review_resign.py` errors
  under parallel execution ('leaked new entries into REPO_ROOT'), passes in isolation."
- A detached full-suite log on this host, the day before the `f0fb` report:
  `14671 passed, 55 skipped, 4 errors in 1:10:59` — all four errors
  `Failed: Test leaked new entries into REPO_ROOT`, on four unrelated unit tests.

## Scope note

Per the operator's scoping call on `f0fb`, the deletion behaviour stays here and is NOT being
changed by `f0fb`'s fix. `f0fb` lands only the additive, non-weakening parts: an honest
`tests/conftest.py` message that names the concurrent-process possibility, `proc.returncode`
in the `tests/e2e/conftest.py` probe diagnostic, and the missing detached-run guidance in
`docs/local-dev-env.md`.

comments.body:
## Scope correction: this is a LOCAL DEV ENVIRONMENT defect, not a shipped-tool concurrency defect

Filed P1 and being lowered to **P2**, with the reasoning recorded so the change is auditable rather
than arbitrary.

### What ships, verified

`pyproject.toml:308` — `packages = ["src/rebar"]`. `tests/` is **not** in the wheel. The offending
fixture `_no_repo_root_leaks` lives at `tests/conftest.py:297`, so **no client ever executes this
code**. The exposure is one developer's working copy during a local test run.

### Why the original framing overstated it

The description reasons from "rebar's ticket store lives under the repo root and rebar writes to it
constantly", which is true, and then treats a fixture deleting such a write as a data-integrity
threat to the store. That conflates two different systems:

- **rebar as a shipped tool, and the `tickets` branch**, whose concurrency handling is robust —
  optimistic concurrency, the bounded write lock, the parent-first cascade, and auto-commit +
  auto-push to `sync.remote` on every write. Nothing in this session challenged any of that. Five
  agents wrote to the store concurrently all day and the store stayed consistent; the only
  observed failures were response TIMEOUTS on writes that had in fact landed.
- **this repository's own test harness**, which is a local development environment with a
  correspondingly small blast radius.

This ticket is entirely the second. The bug is real and worth fixing — a fixture that deletes files
it did not create, with suppressed errors and no attribution, is bad regardless of blast radius —
but it is not a threat to the shipped tool or to anyone's ticket data.

### The bound, stated precisely

Ticket events auto-commit and auto-push on write, so an event that completed its push survives on
the remote even if the local file is removed. The exposure is the window between the write landing
on disk and its push completing, plus local-only state such as `.rebar/workflow_runs` which has no
remote copy. On a developer machine. During a test run. Recoverable by re-fetching.

### What the session added that is genuinely new

Two sibling findings, both also test-harness-local, and one of them arguably worse than the
deletion this ticket was filed for:

1. **Misattribution** (`f0fb`, deterministic reproduction now posted here): the guard does not only
   delete — it FAILS AN INNOCENT TEST and asserts a falsehood ("Test leaked") about a file that
   test never touched. That sends a debugger after the wrong test, which costs more time than the
   deletion costs data.
2. **HEAD-movement errors**: a concurrent `git commit` mid-suite produces
   `Test moved the repo HEAD (<sha> -> <sha>)` errors, observed twice today. Same root condition —
   the harness assumes it is the only actor in the checkout — and it is not yet filed anywhere.

### Consequence for priority

P2, not P1. It is a genuine defect in developer tooling with a bounded, local, recoverable blast
radius, and it should be fixed on that basis rather than on an implied risk to ticket data that
does not survive inspection. Raising it again would need evidence that the shipped tool or a
client's store is reachable, which — per the packaging check above — it is not.

# Phase 1 complete — root cause confirmed at runtime, origin unattributable

## Deterministic reproduction, independently re-run in this worktree (1/1)

Worktree `fix-beagle-leakguard` off `origin/main` at `8fa8f36b64`. A test that sleeps 12s
and touches nothing; a bare `touch` from a separate process 8s in:

    ( sleep 8 && touch $PWD/EXTERNAL_MUTATION_PROBE ) &
    python -m pytest tests/unit/test_zz_probe_tmp.py -q -p no:randomly --no-cov

Observed:

    E  Failed: New entries appeared in REPO_ROOT during this test:
       ['EXTERNAL_MUTATION_PROBE']
    tests/conftest.py:339: Failed
    ERROR tests/unit/test_zz_probe_tmp.py::test_sleeps_and_touches_nothing
    1 passed, 1 error in 12.50s

    $ ls EXTERNAL_MUTATION_PROBE
    ls: ...: No such file or directory

The file created by another process was **gone**. This is a runtime observation of the
mechanism executing, not a reading of the source.

**Timing note worth recording for anyone re-running this.** A first attempt with the touch
1.5s into a 3s test did NOT reproduce: pytest's own startup/collection consumed more than
1.5s, so the external write landed *before* the fixture's `before` snapshot and was absorbed
into the baseline. The window is the test body, not the process lifetime. Use a long-bodied
test and a delay comfortably past collection.

## Proven root cause

`tests/conftest.py:328-338` (`_no_repo_root_leaks`). The fixture computes
`after - before` over `_repo_leak_snapshot(_REPO_ROOT)` and then **unconditionally removes
every entry in that diff** — `shutil.rmtree(target, ignore_errors=True)` for a directory,
`target.unlink()` inside `except OSError: pass` for a file.

The set difference is a statement about *what appeared in a wall-clock window*. Deleting it
is an action premised on a stronger claim — *this test created it* — which the fixture has no
evidence for and, by construction, cannot obtain. Any writer sharing `_REPO_ROOT` produces an
indistinguishable diff entry. The changeable artifact is that deletion block.

## Why this is a defect, not intended behaviour (cited)

Three in-repo authorities, all landed:

1. `tests/_isolation.py:88-102` — `leak_failure_message`'s own docstring, landed today on
   `c9a5388a83` for `f0fb`: "the guard diffs REPO_ROOT around each test, so it cannot tell a
   leak from a write that landed from outside the suite". The repo has already accepted, in
   code, that the guard cannot attribute. The deletion acts on exactly the attribution the
   adjacent message was corrected for asserting.
2. `tests/unit/test_external_mutation_diagnostics.py:38-48` — an existing, passing test
   requiring the guard **not** to assert the test created the entry. Removing the entry is a
   stronger assertion of the same unknowable fact than the sentence that test forbids.
3. `tests/conftest.py:297-310` (`_is_coverage_artifact`) — the repo has already had to patch
   this same "delete a file we did not create" harm once (story `8d36`): coverage workers'
   data files were being deleted by a still-running worker's guard, "corrupting the combine
   (coverage collapses) and spuriously failing that test". That fix was a name-based
   exclusion for one known writer; the general case was left open, and this is it.

Legitimacy: **defect**. Blast radius per the scope-correction comment above: local developer
working copy only (`pyproject.toml:308` ships `packages = ["src/rebar"]`; `tests/` is not in
the wheel).

## Defect origin: UNATTRIBUTABLE — searches recorded

Same conclusion the sibling `f0fb` investigation reached, reached independently here:

- `git blame -w -C -M -L 315,340 -- tests/conftest.py` — the deletion block (lines 328-338:
  `target = _REPO_ROOT / name` through `pass`) blames entirely to **`b534f47a7f9`**,
  2026-06-08, "Extract DSO ticket system + Jira reconciler into standalone rebar".
- `git log -S "shutil.rmtree(target" -- tests/conftest.py` — **exactly one commit**,
  `b534f47a7f9`. The deletion has never been modified in this repository's history.
- `git show -s b534f47a7f9` — no `rebar-ticket:` trailer, no `<id>:` subject. It predates the
  trailer convention.
- `git log --follow --oneline -- tests/conftest.py | tail` — `b534f47a7f9` is the earliest
  commit touching the file. The fixture arrived with the extraction; it was authored in the
  upstream `digital-service-orchestra` plugin, whose history is not in this repo.
- `rebar search` for `no_repo_root_leaks`, `REPO_ROOT leak`, `leak guard` — no originating
  ticket. `git log --grep` finds only *later* repairs to the guard (`91b6994025`
  hurt-brow-swan, `9760b2b27b`, `d8b077451b`, `e23387fd16`, `c9a5388a83`), none of which
  introduced or touched the deletion.

Nothing in this repository's history or tracker can name the change that introduced the
deletion, and the carrier commit is a verbatim import from a repo not present here. Recording
this as **unattributable** rather than charging it to the extraction commit, which carried the
code but did not author the behaviour. The bug will close with `--class=preexisting` and no
`--caused-by`.

## Fix direction (Phase 2)

The burden of proof the description sets — on *keeping* the deletion — is not met. There is
no attribution signal available to the fixture: process ownership of a filesystem entry is
not observable from a snapshot diff, and every candidate proxy (mtime, birthtime, name shape)
is satisfied equally by a concurrent legitimate write. So the deletion is removed rather than
conditioned, and the loud `pytest.fail` is kept: failing on an entry you cannot attribute is
conservative and costs a re-run; deleting on an entry you cannot attribute is irreversible.

AC #3 ("if deletion is retained...") is discharged by not retaining it. The guard keeps
failing on a genuine leak — proven separately, so this is not a silent weakening.

# Phase 2 complete — fix landed for review as Gerrit 1978

## Fix

`tests/conftest.py` — `_no_repo_root_leaks` no longer removes anything. The 11-line
cleanup loop (`shutil.rmtree(target, ignore_errors=True)` / `target.unlink()` under
`except OSError: pass`) is gone; the fixture reports and fails only. In its place is a
comment stating why, addressed to whoever is tempted to restore it: a set difference proves
only that an entry APPEARED, deleting asserts "this test created it", and no obtainable
signal separates the two. The deletion is removed rather than made conditional because there
is nothing to condition it on — mtime, birthtime and name shape are each satisfied equally by
a legitimate concurrent write. `import shutil` drops out with it.

`tests/_isolation.py` — `leak_failure_message` gains one line before the existing two-cause
block: *"They were left on disk untouched — the guard removes nothing, so clean up yourself
once you know which cause applies."* Both existing clauses are byte-identical, so the
properties `test_external_mutation_diagnostics.py` pins (never asserts the test did it; always
offers the external-write cause) are preserved.

`docs/local-dev-env.md` — the detached-run section claimed "It also **deletes** what it
finds, so a file you create mid-run can disappear", which this change makes false. It now
says the guard reports only and that a genuine leak is the reader's to clean up. AC #4 is
also discharged there: the "do not work in that checkout" item now names `rebar` explicitly —
tracker writes land under the checkout (`.rebar/`, `.tickets-*`) and read as new entries, so
**running `rebar` against a worktree while its own suite runs is not supported**.

`_is_coverage_artifact`'s docstring was rewritten by the same change: its rationale was
written in the present tense around deletion, and the combine-corruption harm (story `8d36`)
is now recorded as history rather than as current behaviour.

## RED -> GREEN, with the oracle held out

`tests/unit/test_repo_isolation_guard.py` gains two tests that drive the **real** fixture —
resolved from the live plugin manager, not re-imported — against a `tmp_path` standing in for
REPO_ROOT, so the code under test is the shipped guard rather than the inline pytester copy:

* `test_leak_guard_leaves_entries_it_cannot_attribute_on_disk` — a concurrent writer creates
  a file AND a directory-with-contents mid-test; all three must survive teardown. Covers both
  removal branches.
* `test_leak_guard_still_fails_and_names_every_entry` — the guard must still fail, name every
  entry, and still tell an actually-leaking test to use `tmp_path`.

* **RED** on unmodified `main`, for the right reason:
  `AssertionError: the guard deleted a file it cannot attribute to the test` at the survival
  assertion (not an import or fixture error). The second test was green before and after, by
  design: it is the non-weakening guard.
* **Held out** — the test file was reverted to `main` and declared off-limits before the fix
  subagent started; the subagent reported it never opened it, and self-verified against its
  own scratch reproduction instead.
* **GREEN** after re-applying it: 18 passed across the guard self-test and the external-
  mutation diagnostics.
* **Mutation check** — re-introducing the exact confirmed root cause (the rmtree/unlink loop
  restored verbatim) returns the oracle to **RED** on the same assertion; restoring the fix
  returns it to GREEN. The test has teeth.
* **Refactoring litmus** — the assertions are observable postconditions (a path exists on
  disk; the failure text contains an entry name), not private names or a grep of source.

## AC #2 proven end-to-end as well, not only at the fixture level

A genuinely leaking test seeded into the worktree (`mkdir SEEDED_LEAK_dir` +
`write_text SEEDED_LEAK_file.txt` into REPO_ROOT), run through the real conftest:

    E  Failed: New entries appeared in REPO_ROOT during this test:
       ['SEEDED_LEAK_dir', 'SEEDED_LEAK_file.txt']
    E  They were left on disk untouched — the guard removes nothing, ...
    1 passed, 1 error in 0.53s

Both entries named, and the debris was left on disk (then removed by hand) — the intended new
behaviour. This is not a silent weakening.

## Original report replicated

The Phase-1 reproduction re-run against the fix — external `touch` 8s into a 12s test body:

    1 passed, 1 error in 12.51s
    $ ls -la EXTERNAL_MUTATION_PROBE
    -rw-r--r--  1 joeoakhart  staff  0 Aug 20 23:27 EXTERNAL_MUTATION_PROBE

The file **survives**. The data-loss half of the report is gone. The innocent test is still
errored — that half is not fixable by attribution (the guard genuinely cannot tell), and it is
already mitigated by the message `f0fb` landed, which names the concurrent-write cause instead
of asserting the test leaked.

## Scope and safety

* **Caller-dependency sweep** — `_no_repo_root_leaks` is an autouse fixture with no callers.
  Nothing in the suite asserts the deletion: `git grep` over `_no_repo_root_leaks`,
  `repo_leak_snapshot`, `leak_failure_message` finds only the fixture, the `_isolation`
  primitives, this self-test, and the inline pytester copy — and that copy never deleted, so
  the guard's own end-to-end tests were already written against report-only semantics. Clear.
* **Restoration, not creation** — the change removes behaviour and corrects text. No new entry
  point, artifact, or mutating call.
* **No new dependency** — `import shutil` is removed, none added.
* **No test weakened** — no pre-existing assertion removed, loosened, skipped, or xfailed; the
  diff to existing tests is additive.

## Sibling sweep

* **Construct axis** — the class is "act destructively on shared-checkout state a snapshot
  diff cannot attribute". `grep` for `rmtree` / `.unlink()` across every `tests/**/conftest.py`
  finds exactly two other sites, and both are attributable: `conftest.py:380`
  (`_remove_readonly_run_snapshots`) deletes only under the test's own private `tmp_path`. No
  siblings.
* **Parity axis** — the rule is *a guard reading shared-checkout state must not act
  destructively on state it cannot attribute to the test*. Census of the guards that read
  shared checkout state: `_no_repo_root_leaks` (fixed); `pytest_sessionfinish` porcelain
  backstop (reports only — OK); `_no_repo_commits` (deletes nothing, but its remedy text ends
  in an unconditional `git reset --hard <sha>`, which is destructive advice given for a cause
  it cannot confirm — **MISSING**); `_remove_readonly_run_snapshots` and `_isolate_user_config`
  (N/A, `tmp_path`-scoped); the inline pytester copy in this self-test (N/A, never deleted).
  Disposition for the MISSING slot: filed as `hot-guessable-ungulate`
  (`a991-09dd-aa6a-4a27`), linked `discovered_from` this bug. Left out of this change
  deliberately — it is wording, not behaviour, and keeping this diff tight around the proven
  root cause is worth more than folding it in.

## Gates

* `make lint` — pass (ruff check + format-check + zizmor + actionlint).
* `make typecheck` — pass, 613 source files.
* `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` — `active=49 new=0 increased=0
  stale=0`. (The baseline covers `src/` only; a `tests/` change cannot disturb it.)
* **Full unit + scripts sweep**, CI selection and flags: **12978 passed, 46 skipped**, no
  failures, 8m16s.

## Gerrit

Change **1978** — https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1978

compiled_state.description:
## Problem
`tests/conftest.py`'s autouse `_no_repo_root_leaks` fixture (line 297) **deletes files it did not
create**, using a before/after directory snapshot that cannot distinguish a leaking test from a
concurrent process making a legitimate write.

```python
before = _repo_leak_snapshot(_REPO_ROOT)          # :300
...
after = _repo_leak_snapshot(_REPO_ROOT)           # :304
leaked = {name for name in (after - before) if not _is_coverage_artifact(name)}
for name in sorted(leaked, key=len, reverse=True):
    target = _REPO_ROOT / name
    if target.is_dir():
        shutil.rmtree(target, ignore_errors=True)  # :313
    else:
        target.unlink()                            # :316
```

Anything that appears under `_REPO_ROOT` between the two snapshots is deleted. The fixture's own
comment says cleanup is "best-effort" and suppresses `OSError` so a race cannot mask the real
failure — sound reasoning for the leak it was built to catch, but it means a deletion that hits an
unintended target is **silent**.

## Why this is dangerous in THIS repository specifically
rebar's ticket store lives **under the repo root** (`.tickets-*`), and rebar writes to it constantly
— every `comment`, `edit`, `set-file-impact`, `claim`, `transition`. This project also runs many
agents concurrently, each in its own worktree but frequently issuing `rebar` commands while a suite
runs. A tracker write landing under a worktree's `_REPO_ROOT` during a test is, to this fixture,
indistinguishable from a leak — and gets deleted.

This is not theoretical. Multiple agents in the 2026-08-19/20 session reported this guard firing
because of concurrent `rebar` writes, e.g. "one leak guard tripped because a `rebar transition` wrote
`.rebar/workflow_runs` mid-run", and "`.tickets-tracker` written under that same worktree root
mid-run". Every one of those reports was treated as harmless noise. The deletion half was noticed
only when one agent read the fixture and observed that it **removes** what it flags — so running
rebar tracker writes during a suite in the same worktree is *actively unsafe, not merely noisy*.

## Bounding the damage honestly
Ticket events auto-commit and auto-push to `sync.remote` on write, so an event that completed its
push survives on the remote even if the local file is deleted. The exposure is the window between
the write landing on disk and its push completing — plus any local-only state the fixture removes
(`.rebar/workflow_runs` and similar are not ticket events and have no remote copy).

So this is not "the tracker gets destroyed". It is: a test fixture can silently delete another
process's files, in a repo whose primary datastore lives at that path, with no attribution check and
suppressed errors. The blast radius is bounded by the auto-push, not by the fixture's design.

## The design gap
The fixture asks "what appeared under REPO_ROOT during this test?" when the question it needs is
"what did THIS TEST create?". A snapshot diff cannot answer the second in the presence of any other
writer.

Candidate remedies, to be decided on evidence rather than assumed:
- **Attribute before deleting** — only remove paths the test's own process created, or that match
  the known leak shapes, rather than any diff entry.
- **Fail without deleting** — the `pytest.fail()` already surfaces the leak; deletion is a
  convenience. Removing it converts a silent data-loss risk into a loud, harmless failure. The
  burden of proof should be on keeping the deletion, not on removing it.
- **Exclude the datastore** — never delete under `.tickets-*` / `.rebar/`, on the grounds that no
  legitimate test leak lives there and every legitimate concurrent write does.
- **Detect concurrent writers** and skip cleanup when one is active.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A concurrent, legitimate write under `_REPO_ROOT` during a test run is NOT deleted — proven by
      a test that writes from a separate process mid-test and asserts the file survives.
- [x] The fixture still catches the leak it exists for: a test that genuinely leaks into REPO_ROOT
      still FAILS. Prove it by seeding a leaking test and observing the failure, so this does not
      become a silent weakening of the guard.
- [x] If deletion is retained in any form, deletions are ATTRIBUTED (the fixture can say why it
      believes it created each removed path) and are no longer silent on error.
- [x] Guidance records whether running `rebar` commands against a worktree while its suite runs is
      supported. If it is not, say so in `docs/local-dev-env.md` — several agents did it all session
      believing the resulting errors were cosmetic.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass; `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check`
      reports `new=0 increased=0 stale=0`.

## Provenance
Fixture behaviour read directly at `tests/conftest.py:296-320` on origin/main; the concurrent-write
reports are from four separate agents' own logs during the 2026-08-19/20 session. Surfaced by the
implementer on `dirt-prior-falcon`, which flagged the deletion rather than absorbing it.

file_impact.reason: remove the leak guard's unattributable deletion block
leak_failure_message must state nothing was removed
RED oracle: entries survive teardown, guard still fails
stale claim that the guard deletes what it finds; rebar-during-suite is unsupported
